summary.name: Backup (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining data backup concepts, including repository models, backup methods, storage media, and data management techniques.
use_cases: Planning a backup strategy using the 3-2-1 rule
Choosing between full, incremental and differential backups
Understanding storage media options for archives
Protecting live or open files during backup
Learning how deduplication and compression reduce backup size
summary.what_it_does: The page defines a data backup as a copy of computer data stored elsewhere so it can restore the original after loss. It describes backup methods such as unstructured, full/system imaging, incremental, near-CDP, reverse incremental, and differential. It covers storage media (magnetic tape, hard disk, optical, solid-state, and cloud), the 3-2-1 rule of at least three copies on two media types with one offsite, and storage tiers (online, near-line, offline). It also explains file selection, handling of live data, metadata, compression, and deduplication.
notable: Explains the 3-2-1 backup rule and why ransomware can overwrite connected backup drives
Compares incremental, differential, and reverse incremental backup methods
Covers storage media trade-offs including tape, optical discs, SSDs, and cloud storage
caveats: Describes concepts rather than a specific software product
Page excerpt is cut off before the end of the duplication section
